texts.orig: Why should I spay or neuter my rabbit?
texts.text: Why should I spay or neuter my rabbit?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Many reasons, really. Altered (spayed Or neutered) rabbits avoid uterine and testicular cancer; thereby increasing their lifespan: Altered rabbits are also less likely to exhibit obnoxious behaviors, such as spraying,  fighting and and can be paired with rabbits of the opposite sex for companionship biting

texts.orig: At what age should rabbits be spayed or neutered?
texts.text: At what age should rabbits be spayed or neutered?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Male testicles descend at about 3 1/ months of age, and females reach sexual maturity around 4 months of age. Most veterinarians preferto waitalittlelongerbefore performing surgery to minimize the risks for the rabbit. PHSISPCA has a minimum age limit of 6 months for male rabbits and one year for female rabbits.

texts.orig: How should I prepare my rabbit for surgery?
texts.text: How should I prepare my rabbit for surgery?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Do not fast your rabbit before its surgery Rabbits must have food and water available at all times. If your rabbit is overweight; helshe should be placed on a weight reduction diet, under your veterinarian's supervision.
texts.text: Do not fast your rabbit before its surgery Rabbits must have food and water available at all times. If your rabbit is overweight; helshe should be placed on a weight reduction diet, under your veterinarian's supervision.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: After surgery have your rabbit's cage as usual andseparate him/her from your other pets. Neutered males should not be put in contact with unaltered females for at least three weeks after surgery. Do not encourage any exercise and refrain from picking-up your rabbit unnecessarily: Offer your rabbit what he or she normally eats, as well as "treats" (parsley;   apples, and carrots). Monitor your rabbit's  appetite; but know that he or she may not be interested in food the night after surgery Contact your veterinarian if your rabbit does not eat after 24 hours. Check your rabbit's incision twice a it should be free of blood or discharge. Bruising or swelling of the incisionlscrotum may occur, but it is normal. You may notice that your female rabbit has two small dark lines, one on each side, parallel to her incision These are thin tattoo lines to indicate she has been spayed. If a female her stitches out; call the PHSISPCA Spay & Neuter Clinic for an incision check. ready day pulls
